questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Product Containing a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $v(x)=tan⁡(x).$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\sqrt{x}tan⁡(x))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(\sqrt{x})^{′}\cdot tan⁡(x)+\sqrt{x}\cdot (tan⁡(x))^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}(tan⁡(x))+(\sqrt{x})({sec}^{2}⁡(x)) \\  & =\frac{tan⁡(x)}{2\sqrt{x}}+\sqrt{x}{sec}^{2}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}({e}^{x}cos⁡x)^{′} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =({e}^{x})^{′}\cdot cos⁡x+{e}^{x}\cdot (cos⁡x)^{′} \\  & =({e}^{x})(cos⁡x)+({e}^{x})(-sin⁡x) \\  & ={e}^{x}cos⁡x-{e}^{x}sin⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Product  at a Given Point
questions.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=({x}^{2}-4x+7){e}^{x},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=0$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)={x}^{2}-4x+7$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x-4,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =({x}^{2}-4x+7)\cdot {e}^{x}+{e}^{x}\cdot (2x-4) \\  & ={e}^{x}({x}^{2}-2x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=0$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={{e}^{x}({x}^{2}-2x+3)|}_{x=0} \\  & =1\cdot (0-0+3)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $3.$

questions.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(x-1)ln⁡(4x-3),$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=x-1$ and $v(x)=ln⁡(4x-3).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4}{4x-3}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(x-1)\cdot \frac{4}{4x-3}+ln⁡(4x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=1$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & =(1-1)\cdot \frac{4}{4(1)-3}+ln⁡(4(1)-3) \\  & =0+ln⁡(1)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $0.$

questions.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=xln⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=e.$
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=ln⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =x\cdot \frac{1}{x}+(ln⁡x)\cdot 1 \\  & =1+ln⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=e$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=e} & =1+ln⁡x \\  & =1+ln⁡e \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $2.$

questions.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y={e}^{x}sin⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=sin⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=cos⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot cos⁡x+(sin⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi } & ={{e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x)|}_{x=\pi } \\  & ={e}^{\pi }(-1+0) \\  & =-{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-{e}^{\pi }.$

questions.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(x+2)cos⁡x,$ then the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=x+2$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-sin⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(x+2)\cdot (-sin⁡x)+cos⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =-(x+2)sin⁡x+cos⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\frac{\pi }{2}} & =-(\frac{\pi }{2}+2)sin⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+cos⁡\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =-(\frac{\pi }{2}+2)(1)+0 \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\frac{\pi }{2}-2.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=\cos x .$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\eqalign{
	 (x\cos x)' &=   u'(x) \cdot v(x) + u(x) \cdot v'(x)\
						&= (x)'\cdot \cos x + x\cdot (\cos x)'\
					   & = 1 \cdot \cos x + x (-\sin x)\
					  & =  \cos x - x \sin x					

}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: If a curve $\mathcal C$ is given by $y=e^x\sin x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\dfrac \pi 2.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x) = e^x$ and $v(x)=\sin{x}.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = e^x,\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} = \cos x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot cos⁡x+sin⁡x\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\dfrac\pi 2$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi /2} & ={e}^{\pi /2}(cos⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}(0+1) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $e^{\pi/2}.$
